inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted 673.673m (FY26 Annual Report note 24: 672,747,233 basic + 925,857 dilutive LTIP/SRP/REP rights). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). No DRP has operated since FY22; no buyback since FY20.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt 2,651 = borrowings 2,976 (65 current + 2,911 non-current) - cash 325, FY26 balance sheet (30 Jun 2026). AGL's own net debt of 2,863 adds a 186 AASB-16 lease adjustment and 26 of cross-currency-swap/borrowing-cost adjustments; the lease adjustment is excluded here because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B), the swap adjustment is immaterial (0.04/share) and omitted for consistency with the CSV total_debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report, Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity 'Share-based payments' $2m (FY26) / $2m, plus cash purchase of shares on-market for equity-based remuneration $10m (financing). DB StockBasedComp = 8. Equity-award taxes: none disclosed (Australian filer, no net-share-settlement withholding line). SBC-immaterial market: 0.06% of revenue.
inputs.lease_note: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full FY26 lease cash of $159m (principal $88m in financing + interest $71m in operating, FY26 cash flow statement) is charged inside the cash-adjusted EBITDA margin, and lease liabilities of $1,058m (of which ~$850m are four PPAs restated as leases in FY25 - economically energy-purchase contracts) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax build is ex right-of-use depreciation (~$90m estimated from the $88m principal run-rate; ROU assets $480m).
inputs.last_fcf_formula: owner_fcf = reported_fcf (OCF 1,148 - capex 1,438 = -290) - SBC 8 - lease principal 88 = -386. Lease interest (71), rehabilitation (87), onerous-contract (65) and significant-item (173) cash are already inside OCF. Interest income (12) NOT stripped: AGL is net-debt, there is no cash pile added to EV.
inputs.buyback_note: No on-market buyback since FY20 ($620m). FY26 'purchase of shares on-market for equity-based remuneration' $10m is the cash funding of the SBC charge, already deducted as SBC. Flat count is a modelling convention the company funds via that line.

guidance_fy27.capex: ~1,500 (800 growth + 700 sustaining incl ~500 for two major coal-unit outages)
guidance_fy27.cost_program: $50m annual net operating savings from FY27

inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC: risk-free 4.3% (ACGB 10yr, Sep-2026), ERP 5.5%, equity beta 1.0 (gentailer with wholesale-price and coal-closure exposure; statutory earnings history is highly volatile) -> cost of equity 9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.8% (FY26 net finance costs $375m incl. lease interest on ~$3.1bn average gross debt + leases; AMTN issuance at ~5.5-6%), after-tax 4.1% at 30%. Market weights: equity $5.69bn (673.7m x A$8.45), net debt $2.65bn -> 68/32 -> WACC 7.97%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, coal-closure and execution risk are carried in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate (section 7f: charge risk once).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing table row 2: operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). AGL is an integrated generator/retailer, not a regulated network, REIT, bank or holdco, so the FCF engine applies; section 7 adaptations used: AUD-built WACC (a1), treatment-B leases (b), no NCI (immaterial, $1-2m), no non-operating assets added because no income is stripped (d), SBC kept explicit at 0.06% (e), risk charged once (f). WHY NOT FY26 FCF AS BASE: FY26 owner FCF is -$386m because AGL is in a capex supercycle (FY26 capex $1,438m, FY27 guided ~$1,500m, vs D&A $837m) building 12GW of renewables/firming by 2035 while the coal fleet (Bayswater 2030-33, Loy Yang A 2035) retires. Following the AIA.NZ precedent (component owner-FCF + capex taper) the forward FCF is built from components: a cash-adjusted EBITDA margin anchored to FY27 guidance and the 10-yr underlying-EBITDA-margin average (14.7%), less recurring cash leakage that Underlying EBITDA excludes (rehabilitation ~0.7%, onerous contracts ~0.4%, significant-items/transformation cash ~0.5-1.1%, leases ~1.2% of revenue), a cash-tax rate ramping 18%->30% as accelerated depreciation on the build-out unwinds, and capex tapering from 11.0% of revenue (FY27 guidance) to 6.5% by FY36 as the build-out completes. The 10-year horizon runs to FY36, the year after Loy Yang A's scheduled closure, so the terminal state is the post-coal portfolio. Terminal cap 14x owner FCF (section 4: 12-15x for cyclical/structurally slower businesses; the cap binds in all three scenarios at 8% WACC). EBITDA margin in assumptions is the CASH-ADJUSTED, POST-LEASE margin, not Underlying EBITDA: FY26 = (2,100 - 87 - 65 - 173 - 159) / 13,590 = 11.9%. Statutory NPAT $756m is inflated by derivative fair-value gains; Underlying NPAT $631m is the earnings anchor. Price is the 21-Sep-2026 regular close (16:10 AEST), not after-hours.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Underlying EPS (cents). Statutory EPS CAGRs are undefined: FY2021 (-330.3c) and FY2023 (-187.9c) were impairment-driven losses.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF is negative in FY2025 (-367) and FY2026 (-386): CAGRs undefined. Reported FCF CAGRs are equally undefined. The owner-FCF series FY16-FY26 (AUD m): FY2016: 640, FY2017: 387, FY2018: 1408, FY2019: 678, FY2020: 1389, FY2021: 546, FY2022: 590, FY2023: 287, FY2024: 1398, FY2025: -367, FY2026: -386
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_10yr_cagr (2.0%): AGL's revenue is largely a pass-through of wholesale energy prices and customer numbers; equity CAGR is negative (impairments, DRP) and owner-FCF is negative, so neither can anchor growth. Base revenue growth runs 0% in FY27 (2027 futures -20% in NSW/VIC) then 1.5-2% nominal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR -0.9% vs revenue 5yr CAGR +4.4% and underlying-EPS 5yr CAGR +1.7%: book value shrank on FY21/FY23 onerous-contract and impairment charges (-$2.06bn, -$1.27bn) and a $2.0bn provisions balance. Historical CAGRs describe a coal fleet being written down, not the forward business; the DCF is anchored on FY27 guidance and the 10-yr underlying EBITDA margin average (14.7%), not on any CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is 0.06% of revenue, so owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs would coincide if defined; the wedge is capex, not compensation. Lease principal is only disclosed separately from FY25 (75) and FY26 (88); FY20-FY24 principal was inside 'repayment of borrowings' and is not deducted from those years (understates the deduction by ~$50-70m/yr).

base.ebitda_margin_basis: cash-adjusted post-lease EBITDA margin (Underlying EBITDA less rehabilitation, onerous-contract, significant-items and lease cash)
base.da_pct_basis: D&A ex right-of-use depreciation, % of revenue (FY26: (837-90)/13,590 = 5.5%), rising to 6.5% as a decade of capex above D&A grows the depreciable base; affects only the cash-tax shield

base.wc_capture_basis: receivables + inventory roughly net of payables for an energy retailer; growth consumes a little cash; margin-call swings are timing and excluded

scenario_narratives.base: Wholesale prices soften (2027 NSW/VIC futures -20%) so FY27 revenue is flat and Underlying EBITDA lands mid-guidance (~$2.05bn, 15.1%); thereafter customer growth, electrification and the $50m cost program hold the underlying margin at ~15% (10-yr average 14.7%) while the Liddell/Tomago batteries and Hexham/Tilt PPAs replace the margin lost as Bayswater (2030-33) and Loy Yang A (2035) close. Cash leakage eases from 3.4% of revenue (FY27, transformation overrun) to ~2.8% (rehabilitation rising toward closure, transformation and onerous costs falling away, leases ~1.2%), lifting the cash-adjusted margin from 11.7% to 12.2%. Capex tapers from $1.5bn to ~6.5% of revenue (~$1.1bn) by FY36 as the 12GW build completes with capital partners taking >2GW. Cash tax ramps 18%->30% as accelerated depreciation unwinds. Owner FCF is roughly zero in FY27-28 and reaches ~3.4% of revenue by FY36.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-centre and electrification demand (management's 5 TWh -> 34 TWh pipeline) lifts volumes 3%/yr; battery arbitrage boosts Bayswater returns ~10% and the firming fleet earns premium capacity revenue as coal exits the NEM, taking the underlying margin to ~17% (FY18-19 levels) and the cash-adjusted margin to 14%. Capital partners fund most of the growth pipeline, so capex falls to 6% of revenue by FY35 and owner FCF reaches ~5.5% of revenue. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: New renewable supply and strong plant reliability push wholesale prices down 20%+ and volatility stays suppressed; tier-2 retailers keep taking share (NEM switching 24.4%), so revenue falls 3% in FY27 and drifts up only 1%/yr. Underlying margin compresses to ~12-13% and rehabilitation/closure cash rises as Bayswater and Loy Yang A retire, leaving a 9% cash-adjusted margin. Management trims growth capex but the coal outages and committed projects keep capex above 7% of revenue until FY33. Owner FCF is negative for four years and barely positive at the terminal; with $2.65bn of net debt the equity is worth less than zero on this path - i.e. the bear case requires an equity raise, a dividend cut, or asset sales, which is a finding rather than a rounding detail.

entry_price.method: PV at 15% of the 10 interim owner FCFs + PV at 15% of a terminal value REBUILT at the 15% hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 14x FCF_10)) - net debt, per diluted share; computed per scenario and probability-weighted. No lower-cost exit buyer assumed.
entry_price.note: Negative entry prices mean there is NO price at which the projected flows return 15%: the PV of the flows at the hurdle is below the net debt. The stock cannot meet a 15% hurdle on the base path; only the bull path clears it, and only well below the current price.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 14x)). The 8% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. The 14x cap binds across most of the grid, which is why the terminal-growth columns move little at low WACC; the value is a function of the discount rate and the year-10 FCF, not of g.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 default. Bear raised to 25%: gearing 33.6% and rising, negative FCF two years running, a >40%-wide FY27 NPAT guidance range, a history of $2bn+ coal impairments, and a bear path on which equity value is negative (refinancing/raise risk is real, not cosmetic). Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once - data-centre load materialising, capital partners funding the pipeline, battery arbitrage sustaining thermal returns and wholesale volatility returning - and even then it only reaches the current price.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is 0.06% of revenue (SBC-immaterial market, section 7e): the street basis is only ~$0.20/share above house (PV of ~$8-10m/yr capitalised at 8%/2%), so the accounting-regime band is ~2% of price and the price sits >25x its width above it. band_position is null rather than a meaningless 2,600%.

flags: Bear-case equity value is NEGATIVE (below net debt): the company does not survive the bear path without an equity raise, dividend cut or asset sales.
Base and bear entry prices at a 15% hurdle are negative: no purchase price on those paths returns 15%.
Terminal value is bound by the 14x cap in all three scenarios at 8% WACC (Gordon would be 17-19x).

Weighted IV is far below the market price. The market (EV/underlying EBITDA ~4.0x, P/E 9x underlying, 5.9% franked yield) is capitalising Underlying EBITDA as if the $1.4-1.5bn/yr build-out and ~$0.3bn/yr rehabilitation/onerous/transformation cash were not shareholder costs, or is assuming growth capex earns well above its cost. This DCF charges all of it; the bull case shows what has to be true for A$8.45 to be fair value.
The 10-yr horizon ends FY36, one year after Loy Yang A closes; the terminal capex (6.5%) and leakage (~3.3%) assumptions are the judgment calls that most move the value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Component owner-FCF DCF that charges the full transition capex, coal rehabilitation and lease cash; the value gap to the market is the price the market is paying for the post-coal portfolio and for Underlying EBITDA-based multiples.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
